question: In D&D 5e (SRD 5.2.1), a group of 4 adventurers is ambushed by goblins. Two adventurers were keeping watch and noticed the goblins, but the other two were asleep. How does surprise work in this situation?
expected_answer: The two sleeping adventurers are surprised — they cannot move, take actions, or take reactions until after their first turn ends. The two on watch are NOT surprised and act normally from the first round. The goblins are also not surprised. All creatures still roll initiative normally; the surprised characters simply cannot do anything on their first turn. A member of a group can be surprised even if other members are not.

bm25_simple.answer: SRD 5.2.1 revised rule: Surprise = Disadvantage on Initiative roll, NOT a lost turn. Two watchers: not surprised, roll normally. Two sleepers: surprised, roll Initiative with Disadvantage. Goblins: not surprised, roll normally. Per-creature determination. Source: SRD p.12-13, converting-to-srd-5.2.1.pdf p.1-2.

quality.notes: Correctly identified the SRD 5.2.1 REVISED surprise rule (Disadvantage on Initiative, not lost turn). Faithful to corpus. Expected answer describes old 2014 rules which are not in this corpus.

bm25_2round.answer: SRD 5.2.1 revised surprise: Disadvantage on Initiative, not lost turn. Sleepers also have Unconscious condition (Incapacitated, Prone, Speed 0, auto-fail Str/Dex, crits within 5ft). Both Surprise and Incapacitated give Disadvantage (doesn't stack). Sleepers need to be woken to act. Source: SRD p.12-13, 183-185, 189-191.
